rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause restarts to explain the night’s superiority; its pronoun refers to Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: استئناف مبين لمناط فضلها على تلك المدة المديدة فضمير فيها لليلة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take the pronoun to refer to a thousand months and the clause as their modifier; al-Alusi rejects this as unsound.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الجملة صفة لألف شهر والضمير لها وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify the Spirit as Gabriel, named separately to honor him although he brings the Remembrance.
rows.anchor: الروح عند الجمهور هو جبريل عليه السلام وخص بالذكر لزيادة شرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report describes the Spirit as an immense angel able to swallow the heavens and earth in one bite; al-Alusi leaves its truth to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل ملك عظيم لو التقم السماوات والأرض كان ذلك له لقمة واحدة

rows.speaker: كعب ومقاتل
rows.claim: Kaʿb and Muqatil say the Spirit is a company of angels whom other angels see only on this night, like ascetics seen only on feast days or Fridays.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب ومقاتل الروح طائفة من الملائكة لا تراهم الملائكة إلا تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes the Spirit guardian angels over the angels, analogous to guardian angels over people.
rows.anchor: وقيل حفظة على الملائكة كالملائكة الحفظة علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as created beings who eat and dress but are neither angels nor humans, invoking God’s creation of what people do not know and unknown divine hosts.
rows.anchor: وقيل خلق من خلق الله تعالى يأكلون ويلبسون ليسوا من الملائكة ولا من الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the Spirit as Jesus, who descends to behold this community and visit the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو عيسى عليه السلام ينزل لمطالعة هذه الأمة وليزور النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the spirits of believers descending to visit their families.
rows.anchor: وقيل أرواح المؤمنين ينزلون لزيادة أهليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the Spirit as mercy, by analogy with the reading “God’s mercy”; al-Alusi relies on the Gabriel interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرحمة كما قريء لا تيأسوا من روح الله بالضم وعلى الأول المعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning, supported by reports, is that the angels descend to earth.
rows.anchor: والظاهر الذي تشهد له الأخبار أن التنزل إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the angels descend to greet the believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل ينزلون إليها للتسليم على المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they descend because worship on earth that night is especially meritorious, as travel to Mecca makes worship there more rewarding.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن الله تعالى جعل فضيلة هذه الليلة في الأشتغال بطاعته في الأرض

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIsam al-Din suggests angels descend to apprehend the night since heaven has no night; al-Alusi objects that this does not explain its merit.
rows.anchor: وقال عصام الدين يحتمل أن يكون تنزلهم لأدراكها إذ ليس في السماء ليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting the descent as a descent to the lowest heaven conflicts with the immediately apparent sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد تنزلهم إلى السماء الدنيا وهو خلاف المتبادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A more remote mystical interpretation is that angels leave their lofty absorption in God to greet believers.
rows.anchor: كون المراد بتنزلهم تنزلهم عن مراتبهم العلية من الأشتغال بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi regards all angels as the apparent referent of “the angels.”
rows.anchor: واستظهر أن المراد بالملائكة عليهم السلام جميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the angels are too numerous for earth or the lowest heaven, they may descend in successive groups, like pilgrims entering the Kaaba in turns.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنهم ينزلون فوجا فوجا فمن نازل وصاعد كالحجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The progressive verb “tanazzalu” rather than “nazala” hints at descent in stages.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بتنزل المفيد للتدريج دون نزل رمز إليه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: The suggestion that angels are non-colliding lights is mentioned and dismissed as implausible.
rows.anchor: فالنور إذا ملأ حجرة مثلا لا يمنع من إدخال ألف نور عليه وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict the angels to inhabitants of the Lote Tree, or a subset of them.
rows.anchor: خص الملائكة ببعض فرقهم وهم سكان سدرة النتهى أو بعض منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi resumes a report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas: Gabriel descends with seventy thousand angels carrying light banners, planted at four sacred sites: the Kaaba, the Prophet’s tomb, Jerusalem, and Sinai.
rows.anchor: قال إذا كان ليلة القدر يأمر الله تعالى جبريل عليه السلام أن ينزل إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The angels enter every dwelling, stone, or ship containing a believer, except places with a dog, pig, wine, unlawful ritual impurity, or images; they glorify God and seek forgiveness for Muhammad’s community until dawn.
rows.anchor: ولا يبقى دار ولا حجر ولا بيت ولا سفينة فيها مؤمن أو مؤمنة إلا دخلته الملائكة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On ascent, angels report that God forgave the righteous and accepted their intercession for wrongdoers; the angels of successive heavens praise God in gratitude.
rows.anchor: فيقول جبريل عليه السلام إن الله تعالى غفر لصالحهم وشفعهم في طالحهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report continues with the Lote Tree, gardens, and Throne praising God; the Throne asks about the forgiveness granted the community and is promised incomparable gifts for them.
rows.anchor: إلهي بلغني أنك غفرت البارحة لصالحي أمة محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A report attributed to Kaʿb says all angels of the Lote Tree descend with Gabriel, whose handshake reaches people except drinkers, pork-eaters, and those stained with saffron.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن كعب نزول جميع ملائكة سدرة المنتهى مع جبريل عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: The report takes gooseflesh, a softened heart, and tears as signs that Gabriel shook a person’s hand; al-Alusi asks God to make the reports sound.
rows.anchor: وإن علامة مصافحته عليه السلام اقشعرار الجلد ورقة القلب ودمع العينين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another report has Gabriel distribute mercy first among living believers, then the dead, and finally disbelievers; one touched by it dies in faith by God’s permission.
rows.anchor: قسم على أموات أمة محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيقسم حتى يستغرقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “By their Lord’s permission” may modify “descend” or be an omitted circumstantial qualifier, meaning they descend under God’s command and magnifying the act.
rows.anchor: بإذن ربهم متعلق بتنزل أو بمحذوف وهو حال من فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the angels long for believers on earth and ask permission to descend; al-Alusi sees this as encouragement to strive in worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل الإشارة إلى أنهم يرغبون في أهل الأرض من المؤمنين ويشتاقون إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ desire despite human sins is questioned; one answer is that they do not know the details or do not regard sins as barring their visit.
rows.anchor: واستشكل أمر هذه الرغبة مع كثرة المعاصي وأجيب بأنهم غير واقفين على تفاصيلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are that angels see forms of worship absent in heaven, or wish to hear repentant sinners’ lament; a sacred report says it is dearer than the glorifiers’ clamor.
rows.anchor: أو ليسمعوا أنين العصاة التائبين ففي الحديث القدسي لأنين المذنبين أحب إلي من زجل المسبحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent may reunite angels with the spiritually kindred, since the spirits of the truthful visit angels in their heavenly stations; meeting others is incidental.
rows.anchor: فإن أرواح الصديقين المتجردة عن جلابيب الأبدان لم تزل تزور الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For every matter” means matters determined for the coming year; al-Alusi reports this interpretation from several authorities and takes “min” causally, as “for.”
rows.anchor: من كل أمر أي من أجل كل أمر متعلق به التقدير في تلك السنة إلى قابل

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIsam al-Din asks why angels descend for decrees not carried out until the year; he answers that they receive assignments, not that each angel handles each matter.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت المقدرات لا تفعل في تلك الليلة بل في تمام السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi adds that the descent may prepare recipients to receive what they are commanded, and that the angels’ assignments can be distributed across matters.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون تنزلهم لأعداد القوابل لقبول ما أمروا به

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim takes “min” as “with,” yielding descent with every matter; this may mean good and blessing, or both good and evil, with the preposition causal.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم من بمعنى الباء أي تنزل بكل أمر فقيل أي من الخير والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others read the preposition as association: angels descend while charged with every matter of the coming year, without doing all their assigned work that night.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من جعلها للملابسة والمراد بملابستهم له للأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading would limit the angels to the managing angels, but reports that all kinds descend challenge this restriction.
rows.anchor: والظاهر على ما قالوا أن المراد بالملائكة المدبرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Salam” is a verbal noun meaning safety, fronted as predicate to “it”; its attachment to “from every matter” uses an extended adverbial construction, or a deleted phrase is supplied.
rows.anchor: سلام وهو مصدر بمعنى السلامة خبر مقدم وقوله تعالى هي مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching “from every matter” to “descend” by imagining angels leave their heavenly affairs behind is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل من كل أمر متعلق بتنزل لكن على معنى تنزل إلى الأرض منفصلة من كل أمر لها في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted predicate gives exclusivity, while the nominal predicate intensifies the meaning: the night is as if safety itself.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الخبر للحصر كما في تميمي أنا والأخبار بالمصدر للمبالغة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says God decrees and ordains only safety on this night; al-Alusi suggests this may mean only safety and good are shown to the angels as decreed.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك في معنى ذلك أنه تعالى لا يقدر ولا يقضي فيها إلا السلامة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the night is safe from Satan and his harm; a report says Satan cannot emerge or afflict people with illness, insanity, harm, corruption, or sorcery until dawn.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد أنها سالمة من الشيطان وأذاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that Satan is absent, sins committed that night would arise from the commanding self rather than Satan.
rows.anchor: ولعل ما يصدر من المعاصي على هذا من النفس الأمارة بالسوء لا بواسطة الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi notes the objection that evil occurs nightly and God alone creates it, then proposes that the meaning is that only safety and good are manifested to the angels.
rows.anchor: إنما يقدر في هذه الليلة السلامة والخير أي لا يظهر سبحانه للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the night itself a complete means of salvation from the Resurrection’s dangers, since worshippers who pray it in faith and hope are forgiven prior sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما هي إلا سلامة على نحو ما رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إلا رحمة

rows.speaker: الشعبي ومنصور
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and Mansur report that “salam” means greetings: the night is filled with angels saluting believers.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن الشعبي ومنصور وجعلها عين التسليم للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Until the break of dawn” marks safety or greetings as lasting through the whole night; “maṭlaʿ” is primarily a time noun, though a verbal noun is also possible with an understood time-word.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى حتى مطلع الفجر غاية تبين تعميم السلامة أو التسليم كل الليلة

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi and others say the endpoint must be construed as “safe” or “saluted” for attachment to be valid; others allow separation between a verbal noun and its complement.
rows.anchor: وأفاد الطبرسي وغيره أنه لا بد من تأويله بسالمة أو مسلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the endpoint to the angels’ descent, with waves continuing until dawn, is strained because “it is safety” intervenes and is not parenthetical.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه تعسف لأن سلام هي أجنبي وليس باعتراض

rows.speaker: الطيبي والطبرسي
rows.claim: A proposed pause after “salam” would make it a predicate of an omitted subject and “until dawn” the predicate of “it”; al-Tibi, al-Tabarsi, and others disallow this parsing.
rows.anchor: ولم يجوز ذلك الطيبي والطبرسي وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though every night lasts to dawn, the phrase clarifies that this night shares ordinary nights’ duration despite differing in merit, removing a possible misunderstanding after its superiority to a thousand months is stated.
rows.anchor: وكان مظنة توهم أن ذاتها في المقدار مغايرة لذوات الليالي فيه أيضا دفع ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿIkrima, and al-Kalbi read “min kulli imriʾ” with a final hamza: descent is for each person and what is decreed for them, or for the believers’ benefit through forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة والكلبي من كل امريء بهمز في آخره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: If the phrase attaches to “salam,” this reading can mean that each angel gives greetings and congratulations to believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل الجار والمجرور متعلق بسلام والمراد بكل امريء الملائكة

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim rejects the reading “imriʾ” with hamza.
rows.anchor: وأنكر كما قال ابن جني هذه القراءة أبو حاتم

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء والأعمش وابن وثاب وطلحة وابن محيصن والكسائي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These readers, with a variant transmission from Abu ʿAmr, read “maṭliʿ” with kasra: it may be a verbal noun or an irregular time noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء والأعمش وابن وثاب وطلحة وابن محيصن والكسائي وأبو عمرو بخلاف عنه مطلع بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr reports the regional distinction that for Hijazis the kasra form marks the place of rising and the fatha form the verbal noun; Tamim uses both as verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وقيل المصدر بالفتح وموضع الطلوع بالكسر عند أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha asks what to say if she finds Laylat al-Qadr; the Prophet teaches the supplication asking God, the Pardoner who loves pardon, to pardon her. Al-Tirmidhi authenticates the report.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت قلت يا رسول الله إن وافقت ليلة القدر فما أقول

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says prayer is especially beloved on that night, while reciting and making supplication is also good.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان الثوري في تلك الليلة أحب من الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن رجب
rows.claim: Ibn Rajab calls it most complete to combine prayer, recitation, supplication, and reflection; the Prophet did all these, especially in the final ten nights, reading slowly and seeking refuge or mercy at the corresponding verses.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن رجب أن الأكمل الجمع بين الصلاة والقراءة والدعاء والتفكر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the night’s devotional vigil is achieved by performing tarawih prayer.
rows.anchor: ويحصل قيامها على ما قال البعض بصلاة التراويح

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that whoever prays Maghrib and ʿIsha in congregation through Ramadan receives an abundant share of Laylat al-Qadr; al-Bayhaqi transmits it.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من صلى المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says that attending the ʿIsha congregation on Laylat al-Qadr secures one’s share of it; several compilers transmit this.
rows.anchor: وأخرج مالك وابن شيبة وابن زنجوية والبيهقي عن سعيد بن المسيب قال من شهد العشاء ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami says someone who sees the night should keep it secret; its full merit belongs only to one whom God has shown it.
rows.anchor: وفي تحفة المحتاج لابن حجر الهيتي عليه الرحمة يسن لرائيها كتمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi understands seeing the night as perceiving its distinctive lights or the angels’ descent, or receiving a disclosure that yields knowledge; this implies God may let some servants see it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه عني برؤيتها رؤية ما يحصل به العلم له بها

rows.speaker: أبو حفص بن شاهين
rows.claim: Ibn Shahin’s account says only Muhammad was shown the night: God identified it in a dream, but after two men quarreled he forgot it and was told to seek it in the final ten nights; others would never see it directly.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حفص بن شاهين على ما حكاه ابن رجب أن الله تعالى لم يكشفها لأحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi accepts as unquestionably sound the report that the Prophet saw and then forgot the night, but doubts the claim that neither he nor anyone in his community saw it thereafter.
rows.anchor: وحديث أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم رآها ونسيها وقد رواه الإمام مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek the night in the last ten suggests that seeing it then remains possible, since people are not normally told to seek what cannot be hoped for.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأمر بالتماسه في العشر الأواخر مثلا يشير إلى رجاء رؤيتها فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that two Companions dreamed the night fell in the last seven nights; the Prophet said their dreams agreed and instructed people to seek it then.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار ما يدل على أن رؤيتها مناما وقعت لغيره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says the night exists and can be seen and recognized each Ramadan by whomever God wills, as abundant reports and pious experiences attest.
rows.anchor: في شرح الصحيح للنووي اعلم أن ليلة القدر موجودة وأنها ترى ويتحققها من شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Al-Qadi ʿIyad’s quotation of al-Muhallab, that the night cannot truly be seen, is called a gross error by al-Nawawi and al-Alusi.
rows.anchor: وأما قول القاضي عياض عن المهلب بن أبي صفرة لا يمكن رؤيتها حقيقة فغلظ فاحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If horizons differ, the night could be odd for some and even for others, or daytime for some while night for others; there is no universally fixed date, night, or Ramadan boundary.
rows.anchor: يلزم القول بتعددها في رمضان وكونها وترا من لياليه عند قوم وشفعا عند آخرين

rows.speaker: بعض
rows.claim: One response accepts that descriptions such as odd-numbered night, a particular date, and night apply relative to each population’s horizon and its local night.
rows.anchor: وأجاب بعض بالتزام أن ما أطلق من القول فيها ليس على إطلاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-name reflects the location where the Qur’an was revealed and the majority of believers, rather than places where that interval is daytime.
rows.anchor: وأن التعبير بالليلة لرعاية مكان المنزل عليه القرآن عليه الصلاة والسلام وغالب المؤمنين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi finds the differing-horizon problem serious and outside rational resolution; some other proposed answer is too awkward to state, while he has not located Ibn ʿAjluni’s treatment of it.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن البحث قوي والأمر مما لا مجال لعقلي فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same difficulty applies to God’s descent to the lowest heaven, the Friday hour of response, and other times of worship; Ibn Taymiyya discussed the former and Ibn Hajar the latter.
rows.anchor: ومثل ليلة القدر فيما ذكر وقت نزوله سبحانه وتعالى إلى السماء الدنيا من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility makes the night local: it begins at each place’s sunset, so it starts later in Istanbul than Baghdad, and angels descend for each people at its onset and ascend at dawn.
rows.anchor: وربما يقال أنها لكل قوم ليلتهم وإن اختلفت دخولا وخروجا بالنسبة إلى آفاقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, angels may remain until night has ended throughout the inhabited world; on either account decrees and its merit apply to each locality as its own night arrives.
rows.anchor: أو يبقى المتنزل منهم هناك إلى أن تنقضي الليلة في جميع المعمورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi offers this local-night account as his best thought on the problem, while noting that many conflicting reports have contested authenticity.
rows.anchor: وهذا غاية ما يخطر بالبال فيما يتعلق بهذا الإشكال

rows.speaker: السادة الصوفية
rows.claim: For Sufi masters, Laylat al-Qadr is when a spiritual wayfarer receives a special unveiling of their rank in relation to the Beloved and begins attaining the station of perfected knowers.
rows.anchor: ثم إن ليلة القدر عند السادة الصوفية ليلة يختص فيها السالك بتجبل خاص يعرف به قدره

rows.speaker: ابن الفارض
rows.claim: Ibn al-Farid’s verse says every night becomes Laylat al-Qadr when nearness arrives, just as every day of meeting becomes Friday.
rows.anchor: وكل الليالي ليلة القدر إن دنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is also called al-Qiyama, al-Balad, al-Munfakkin, al-Bariyya, and Lam Yakun, as al-Bahr notes.
rows.anchor: وتسمى سورة القيامة وسورة البلد وسورة المنفكين وسورة البرية وسورة لم يكن

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Reports disagree about whether it is Meccan or Medinan: al-Bahr gives the majority as Meccan, while Ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAta ibn Yasar call it Medinan, as does al-Tahrir, which also calls that the majority view.
rows.anchor: قال في البحر مكية في قول الجمهور وقال ابن الزبير وعطاء بن يسار مدنية

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is Meccan, a choice also made by Yahya ibn Sallam; Ibn al-Faras says Meccan is more likely and relates that view from ʿAisha.
rows.anchor: وروي أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنها مكية واختاره يحيى بن سلام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir decisively regards it as Medinan, citing a report about its revelation and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: وجزم ابن كثير بأنها مدنية واستدل على ذلك

rows.speaker: أبو خيثمة البدري
rows.claim: Abu Khaythama al-Badri reports that Gabriel commanded the Prophet to recite the newly revealed sura to Ubayy; Ubayy wept when told he had been named. Al-Alusi calls this the sounder view.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب إلى آخرها قال جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Basran count gives the sura nine verses, while other regional counts give eight.
rows.anchor: وآيها تسع في البصري وثمان في غيره

rows.speaker: إسماعيل بن أبي حكيم عن مطر المزني أو المدني
rows.claim: A report on its merit says God addresses the one who recites “Lam yakun,” promising to grant Paradise until the servant is content and asking nothing from them in either life.
rows.anchor: وجاء في فضلها ما أخرجه أبو موسى المديني في المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura follows the previous one by giving a reason for the Qur’an’s revelation: disbelievers would not leave disbelief until the proof, a messenger reciting purified pages, came to them.
rows.anchor: ووجه مناسبتها لما قبلها إن قوله تعالى فيها لم يكن الذين الخ كالتعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those who disbelieved from the People of the Book” means Jews and Christians; naming them this way may emphasize the gravity of their disbelief or signal their scriptural knowledge of the promised truth.
rows.anchor: لم يكن الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب أي اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense description treats their disbelief as arising after their prophets, in separate instances.
rows.anchor: وإيراد الصلة فعلا لما أن كفرهم حادث بعد أنبيائهم عليهم السلام بالآحاد

rows.speaker: أبو منصور الماتريدي
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi takes “min” partitively, not as explanatory, since some Christians, including Melkites, remained in true belief until Muhammad’s mission or their deaths.
rows.anchor: ومن للتبعيض كما قال علم الهدى الشيخ أبو منصور الماتريدي في التأويلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that explanatory “min” entails all had disbelieved beforehand is answered by identifying them as disbelievers in light of their state after the mission.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض لا نسلم أن التبيين يقتضي كفر جميعهم قبل البعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas takes the People of the Book here as the Jewish tribes around Medina: Qurayza, al-Nadir, and Qaynuqaʿ.
rows.anchor: وأيد إرادة التبعيض بما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists are those who assign God a partner, an idol or other being; some restrict the referent to idol-worshipping Arab polytheists around Mecca and Medina, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbas.
rows.anchor: والمشركين وهم من اعتقدوا الله سبحانه شريكا صنما أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking “the polytheists” as the People of the Book because they call Jesus or Ezra God’s son, coordinated only by a difference in label, is rejected.
rows.anchor: واحتمال أن يراد بالمشركين أهل الكتاب وشركهم لقولهم المسيح ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading nominates “al-mushrikun” in coordination with the relative pronoun; parsing the common genitive reading as mere attraction is also discussed.
rows.anchor: وقريء والمشركون بالرفع عطفا على الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from the People of the Book and the polytheists” functions circumstantially with “disbelieved.”
rows.anchor: والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال من ضمير كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Munfakkin” is the predicate of “yakun”; it means leaving the state they held, and is the active participle of intransitive “infakka.”
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى منفكيم خبر يكن والأنفكاك في الأصل افتراق الأمور

rows.speaker: بعض النحاة
rows.claim: Some grammarians derive the participle from defective “infakka” and posit an omitted predicate such as promising to follow truth; al-Alusi objects that a kāna predicate cannot ordinarily be omitted.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعض النحاة أنه وصف منها والخبر محذوف أي واعدين اتباع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Until the clear proof comes” attaches to “munfakkin”; “bayyina” may mean one who makes truth clear or a proof establishing a claim, understood as a miracle.
rows.anchor: والبينة صفة اسم الفاعل أي المبين للحق أو هي بمعناها المعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A messenger” is apposition to “the clear proof,” or a predicate to an omitted subject; the indefinite form magnifies him, and he is the Prophet Muhammad.
rows.anchor: رسول بدل منها بدل كل من كل أو خبر لمقدر أي هي رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From God” modifies the messenger and adds a further distinction, reinforcing the honor already conveyed by the indefinite form.
rows.anchor: وقوله سبحانه من الله في موضع الصفة له مفيد للفخامة الإضافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Reciting purified pages” may modify the messenger or be circumstantial for the pronoun in the preceding modifier.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى يتلوا صحفا مطهرة صفة له أو حال من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In them are upright writings” is a second modifier or circumstantial clause for the pages; alternatively only the prepositional phrase modifies them and “books” is its subject.
rows.anchor: فيها كتب قيمة صفة ثانية لصحفا أو حال من الضمير في صفتها الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger himself may be the proof because his character reached a miraculous degree, as al-Ghazali argues; al-Busiri’s verse points to his knowledge despite illiteracy and orphanhood, and other miracles also qualify.
rows.anchor: كما قال الغزالي في المنقذ من الضلال وأشار إليه البوصيري بقوله

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatada and Ibn Zayd report that the proof is the Qur’an, which clarifies truth or stands as a miracle establishing the claim.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالبينة القرآن لأنه مبين للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make “messenger” an appositive with an understood noun such as proof, revelation, miracle, or book; or a predicate with the recitation clause explaining the proof, an aside praising it, or a modifier meaning the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ورسول عليه قيل بدل اشتمال أو بدل كل من كل أيضا بتقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
rows.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allah read “rasulan” in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative describing the proof.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله رسولا بالنصب على الحالية من البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pages are sheets of writing; purifying them is a metaphor for their freedom from falsehood, or a metaphorical image of purity, or a transferred description implying only the purified touch them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتطهيرها تنزيهها عن الباطل على سبيل الأستعارة المصرحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Books” means written contents, and “upright” means straight in their proclamation of truth; al-Taysir says they are prophetic scriptures confirmed by the Qur’an, as if contained in it.
rows.anchor: وبالقيمة المستقيمة واستقامتها نطقها بالحق وفي التيسير هي كتب الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reciting pages despite being unable to read is a metonymy referring to the content he recites; other proposals supply “like pages” or use metaphor and the pages for their contents.
rows.anchor: ووصفه عليه الصلاة والسلام بتلاوة الصحف المذكورة بناء على المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative identifies the messenger as Gabriel and the pages as angelic copies from the Preserved Tablet, but turning “pages” into revelation is weak; al-Alusi prefers Muhammad, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil.
rows.anchor: والأولى حمل الرسول على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وهو المروي عن ابن عباس ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi calls the passage among the Qur’an’s hardest in structure and exegesis: reading it as pre-mission disbelief seems to say they stopped disbelieving when the Messenger came, contrary to what follows.
rows.anchor: حتى قال الواحدي في كتاب البسيط أنها من أصعب ما في القرآن نظما وتفسيرا

rows.speaker: جار الله
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says both groups claimed they would not leave their religions until the promised Prophet described in Torah and Gospel arrived; the next verse rebukes them for then separating from truth.
rows.anchor: قال جار الله كان الكفار من الفريقين يقولون قبل المبعث لا ننفك عما نحن فيه

rows.speaker: جار الله
rows.claim: Zamakhshari likens their conduct to a sinful poor person who vows to stop sinning once rich, then becomes more sinful after receiving wealth: the first verse quotes their claim and the next exposes its outcome.
rows.anchor: وحاصله أن الأول من باب الحكاية لزعمهم وقوله سبحانه وما تفرق الخ إلزام عليهم

rows.speaker: جار الله
rows.claim: On this reading, their “separation” is departure from truth and persistence in disbelief; the polytheists are omitted from the verse because their case follows a fortiori.
rows.anchor: وظاهره أنه أراد بتفرقهم تفرقهم عن الحق وحمل على على الكفر والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related reading says they kept their pledge to believe in the promised last messenger until the condition they had set arrived, as the following verse describes their division.
rows.anchor: أي لم يكونوا منفكين عما كانوا عليه من الوعد باتباع الحق والإيمان بالرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book were known to seek victory through the coming Prophet; some polytheists may have accepted this belief, including Zayd ibn ʿAmr, who sought an Arab prophet from Quraysh and Hashim.
rows.anchor: حتى أنهم كانوا يستفتحون ويقولون اللهم افتح علينا وانصرنا بالنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present form “comes” reflects the tense of the reported claim, as in a Qur’anic expression using a present verb for a past event.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن إتيانه بصيغة المضارع حال المحكي لا باعتبار حال الحكاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 4 especially censures the People of the Book because the truth was clear and they had full access to their scripture and its prophecies; their prior generic designation had included both groups.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى وما تفرق الخ كلام مسوق لمزيد التشنيع على أهل الكتاب خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although both groups had agreed in the prior claim, “not breaking away” describes their common position ending, while “separating” describes its fracture into their longstanding differences.
rows.anchor: عبر عما صدر منهم عقيب الأتفاق عند الأخبار بوقوعه بالأنفكاك

rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar reads: they did not cease disbelieving even when the proof came. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi objects that “until” cannot mean “even though” in Arabic; an omitted “at any time” is also problematic.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي عبد الجبار المعنى لم يكن الذين كفروا منفكين عن كفرهم وإن جاءتهم البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they praised the Prophet until he came, then split and spoke falsely about him; al-Alusi objects that this assumes an unstated complement for “not ceasing.”
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لم يكونوا منفكين عن ذكر الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بالمناقب والفضائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the Prophet’s arrival made some believe and others persist, satisfying the endpoint; al-Alusi objects that the next verse condemns all and explicitly speaks of disbelievers among them.
rows.anchor: ويكفي ذلك في العمل بموجب حتى وتعقب بأن ظاهر وما تفرق الخ ذم لجميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they were certain in their religions until the Prophet came, when their thoughts became unsettled and doubtful; al-Alusi finds this unsatisfactory.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى لم يكونوا منفكين عن كفرهم بأن يترددوا فيه بل كانوا جازمين به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lexical interpretation makes “munfakkin” mean destroyed, by analogy with a childbirth injury; it yields that they were not punished or alive only until proof came, which al-Alusi dismisses.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى منفكين هالكين من قولهم انفك صلا المرأة عند الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says they did not leave their religion until the Messenger’s pages showed its abrogation, after which they only adhered to it outwardly; al-Alusi says it is weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد أنهم لم ينفكوا عن دينهم حقيقة إلى مجيء الرسول

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the groups remained together in their distinct religions until the proof came, then separated as each asserted its own position; al-Alusi objects that the proof should have united them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان الظاهر أن المعنى لم يكونوا منفكين أي منفصلا بعضهم عن بعض

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya proposes that people were never outside God’s command, power, and oversight before a messenger was sent, since people are not left purposeless.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ههنا وجه بارع المعنى وذلك أن يكون المراد لم يكن هؤلاء القوم منفكين من أمر الله تعالى وقدرته

rows.speaker: القائلون بمفهوم الغاية
rows.claim: The apparent contradiction assumes that an endpoint implies a changed state afterward, a principle held by most jurists and theologians including Qadi Abu Bakr, Qadi ʿAbd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri.
rows.anchor: مبني على مذهب القائلين بمفهوم الغاية وهم أكثر الفقهاء وجماعة من المتكلمين

rows.speaker: أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Hanafis and other jurists and theologians deny that an endpoint carries this implication; al-Amidi chose their position and argued against opposing evidence.
rows.anchor: دون مذهب القائلين به وهم أصحاب الإمام أبي حنيفة وجماعة من الفقهاء والمتكلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “they were commanded only to worship God” is circumstantial and intensifies the ugliness of their conduct; command means general obligation, its object is omitted, and the purposive exception means worship was the sole purpose of their charge.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله جملة حالية مفيدة لغاية قبح ما فعلوا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Arabs use “li” where “an” appears in commands and expressions of will; accordingly this may mean “only that they worship,” making worship itself the commanded act. Al-Alusi prefers the purpose reading.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء العرب تجعل اللام موضع أن في الأمر كأمرنا لنسلم

rows.speaker: أبو منصور الماتريدي
rows.claim: Al-Maturidi says this clarifies “I created jinn and humans only to worship Me”: it means God charged them to worship so that the obedient and disobedient might be distinguished; al-Alusi praises the subtle solution.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية علم منها معنى قوله تعالى وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sincerely devoting religion to Him” means making worship exclusive to God and avoiding association; “religion” is the object, though other syntax supplies an omitted object or an omitted preposition.
rows.anchor: مخلصين له الدين أي جاعلين دينهم خالصا له تعالى فلا يشركون به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan’s reading with fatḥa on the lām, “mukhliṣīn,” requires taking “religion” as the object of worship or as an accusative verbal noun rather than a direct object of “sincere.”
rows.anchor: وقراءة الحسن مخلصين بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Hunafaʾ” means turning from deviant doctrines toward Islam and reinforces sincerity; ḥanaf is inclination toward straightness, while the crooked-foot usage may be an auspicious inversion or a double metonymy.
rows.anchor: حنفاء أي مائلين عن جميع العقائد الزائغة إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets “hunafaʾ” as pilgrims; Qatada as circumcised and forbidding marriage to mothers and close kin; Abu Qilaba as believers in all the prophets.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس تفسير حنفاء هنا بحجاجا وعن قتادة بمختتنين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes “hunafaʾ” to mean following Abraham’s religion; al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says facing the qibla in prayer, and another view says gathering all religion.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد بمتبعين دين إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish prayer and pay alms is direct if those rites existed in their law; if they refer to Islamic rites, their earlier command to follow the new law includes them.
rows.anchor: إن أريد بهما ما في شريعتهم من الصلاة والزكاة فالأمر بهما ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to worshipping God sincerely, prayer, and almsgiving; the distant demonstrative signals their lofty rank and honor.
rows.anchor: وذلك إشارة إلى كا ذكر من عبادة الله تعالى بالأخلاص

rows.speaker: محمد بن الأشعث الطالقاني
rows.claim: Al-Talqani reads “the upright religion” as the upright books, linked by the definite article to the books of verse 3.
rows.anchor: دين القيمة أي الكتب القيمة فأل للعهد إشارة إلى ما تقدم في قوله تعالى فيها كتب قيمة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says “the upright” means the upright community; others take it as the upright religious way or “millah,” with the difference between religion and community making the annexation valid.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج أي الأمة القيمة أي المستقيمة وقال غير واحد أي الملة القيمة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “al-din al-qayyimati”; the feminine ending either treats religion as “millah” or intensifies the meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله رضي الله تعالى عنه الدين القيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse explains both groups’ afterlife fate after their worldly state; mentioning polytheists prevents readers from supposing the punishment applies only to the People of the Book because they alone saw scriptural signs of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قيل بيان لحال الفريقين في الآخرة بعد بيان حالهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being in Hell means they will enter it, with nominal syntax marking certainty; alternatively the phrase means they are already in its cause, disbelief, or that disbelief is the present form of their future fire.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كونهم في نار جهنم أنهم يصيرون إليها يوم القيامة لكن لتحقق ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both groups enter Hell eternally, but their punishment differs by degree: polytheists occupy a lower tier because their shirk is worse, despite the People of the Book knowingly rejecting the Prophet.
rows.anchor: واشتراك الفريقين في دخول النار بطريق الخلود لا ينافي تفاوت عذابهما في الكيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is used as evidence that disbelievers remain in the Fire forever.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بالآية على خلود الكفار مطلقا في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” refers to people characterized by the listed abominations; “worst of creation” may mean worst in deeds, explaining their punishment, or worst in rank and destination, emphasizing it. Al-Alusi favors the first as parallel to the believers’ description.
rows.anchor: والمراد قيل هم شر البرية أعمالا فتكون الجملة في حيز التعليل لخلودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal superlative is questioned because hypocrites are also condemned to Hell’s lowest level; another suggestion that Pharaoh or the camel-killer could be worse still leaves a problem.
rows.anchor: قال سبحانه أن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difficulty disappears if the claim is relative to believers as imagined by the disbelievers: they are the worst creatures other than the believers.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن ذلك إذا كان الحصر حقيقيا وأما إذا كان إضافيا بالنسبة إلى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view limits “bariyya” to humanity and says these disbelievers are worst in human deeds because they knowingly rejected the Prophet’s signs and caused later people to doubt, while distorting scripture and obstructing him; their deeds exceeded Pharaoh’s and the camel-killer’s.
rows.anchor: وقيل يراد بالبرية البشر ويراد بشريتهم بحسب الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes the disbelievers as all people across history, not just those first mentioned; al-Alusi notes it requires taking “creation” as humankind.
rows.anchor: وقيل ليس المراد بأولئك الذين كفروا أقواما مخصوصين

rows.speaker: الأعرج وابن عامر ونافع
rows.claim: Al-Aʿraj, Ibn ʿAmir, and Nafiʿ read “al-bariʾa” with hamza here and in the following verse, deriving it from God’s creating and meaning creatures.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وابن عامر ونافع البريئة هنا وفيما بعد بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza-less form may derive separately from “dust,” hence refer to humans; alternatively the two readings share the meaning humans or differ between all creatures and humans born of soil.
rows.anchor: وقيل ليس بالأصل وإنما البرية بغير همز من البري المقصور يعني التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither reading is erroneous: both are transmitted from sound authorities, and the hamza is also part of the language of the Prophet’s people.
rows.anchor: فليست القراءة خطأ كيف وقد نقلت عمن ثبتت عصمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ description follows the disbelievers’ as Qur’anic practice pairs warning with encouragement; another interpretation makes verse 6 confirm the upright religion by showing opposite outcomes for refusal and compliance.
rows.anchor: بيان لمحاسن أحوال المؤمنين أثر بيان سوء حال الكفرة جريا على السنة القرآنية

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIsam al-Din says separating the believers’ sentence avoids suggesting a mismatch between its subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: وكأنه فصل لتخييل عدم المناسبة بين الجملتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” refers to people possessing the utmost honor through faith and obedience; Hamid and ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd al-Wahid read “khiyar,” the chosen or best, instead of “khayr.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حميد وعامر بن عبد الواحد هم خيار البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their gardens recompense their faith and obedience; calling them the best first, then specifying their reward from their nurturing Lord, multiplied gardens, rivers, and everlasting life, expresses their supreme state.
rows.anchor: جزاؤهم بمقابلة ما لهم من الإيمان والطاعات عند ربهم جنات عدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straightforward syntax makes “they are the best of creation” and the following clause nominal sentences; another view makes the first clause parenthetical to balance the preceding statement, which al-Alusi questions.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن جملة هم خير البرية اسم الإشارة وكذا ما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God is pleased with them” independently announces an additional divine favor; it may instead explain whether they have anything beyond the stated reward, serve as another predicate or circumstantial clause, or figuratively express honor by God’s action. The prayer reading is unlikely beside “they are pleased with Him.”
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى رضي الله عنهم استئناف نحوي وإخبار عما تفضل عز وجل به زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their satisfaction is explained by attaining the furthest goals and receiving what no eye has seen, ear heard, or heart imagined.
rows.anchor: وعلل رضاهم بأنهم بلغوا من المطالب قاصيتها ومن المآرب ناصيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is for whoever fears his Lord” refers to reward and approval; fear is the foundation of real happiness because it keeps people from sins and prepares them for judgment.
rows.anchor: ذلك أي ما ذكره من الجزاء والرضوان لمن خشى ربه فإن الخشية ملاك السعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The link to fear also recalls that only the learned among God’s servants fear Him; al-Junayd says satisfaction corresponds to strength of knowledge and rootedness in recognition.
rows.anchor: وإنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء ولذا قال الجنيد قدس سره الرضا على قدر قوة العلم

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIsam al-Din takes “that” to refer to faith and righteous action that produce reward and divine approval; al-Alusi objects that this neglects the preceding links and makes the final qualification nearly pointless.
rows.anchor: وقال عصام الدين الأظهر أن ذلك إشارة إلى ما يترتب عليه الجزاء والرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “Lord” evokes ownership and nurturing as grounds for fear and warns against being deceived by divine forbearance.
rows.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية المعربة عن المالكية والتربية للأشعار بعلة الخشية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a Prophetic argument that the faithful servant’s rank with God on Judgment Day exceeds an angel’s, citing verse 7 as proof that believers are the best creation.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا أتعجبون لمنزلة الملائكة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits from ʿAisha that the Prophet answered her question about the most honored creation by reciting verse 7.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن عائشة قالت قلت يا رسول الله من أكرم الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The superiority argument treats “creation” as all creatures and must include prophets among the believers; otherwise ordinary believers would outrank elite angelic messengers, a view Sunnis reject. Al-Razi’s objections are debatable; a safer reading makes the comparison relative to what disbelievers claim.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن هذا ظاهر في أن المراد بالبرية الخليقة مطلقا ليتم الأستدلال
